parts.label: (a)
hints: Hint 1: Think about units - if you multiply a velocity in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ by a time in $\text{s}$, what quantity with what unit do you get?
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Link Area to Multiplication**
Think of the small strip of area as $v$ multiplied by $t$. Since velocity is the rate of change of position, adding up $v \times \Delta t$ for all the little time intervals adds up all the little bits of position change.

parts.label: (b)(i)
key_concepts: gradient of velocity-time graph equals acceleration
hints: Hint 1: Look closely at Fig. 3.2 for trolley B. During which time interval is its velocity changing, and what does that tell you about when the collision is happening?
Hint 2: Pick two clear points on that sloping straight section, read off the change in $v$ and the change in $t$, and divide the change in velocity by the time taken.
parts.proper_answer: $a = 0.90\text{ m s}^{-2}$ in the direction of motion.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Spot the Collision on the Graph**
You are sitting with Fig. 3.2. From $t = 0$ to $t = 0.15\text{ s}$ the graph is flat at $0.12\text{ m s}^{-1}$, so B moves at constant velocity. From $t = 0.15\text{ s}$ to $t = 0.35\text{ s}$ the velocity rises steadily from $0.12$ to $0.30\text{ m s}^{-1}$. That sloping part is the collision when A pushes B forward. After $t = 0.35\text{ s}$ it is flat again, so the collision is over.

Step 2: **Use Gradient Equals Acceleration**
For a $v$-$t$ graph, gradient is acceleration:
$$a = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} = \frac{v - u}{t}$$
Take e.g. $u = 0.12\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $t = 0.15\text{ s}$ and $v = 0.30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $t = 0.35\text{ s}$:
$$a = \frac{0.30 - 0.12}{0.35 - 0.15} = \frac{0.18}{0.20} = 0.90\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

parts.label: (b)(ii)
hints: Hint 1: Resistive forces are negligible and the trolleys collide, so think about what total quantity for the A + B system must stay the same before and after.
Hint 2: Write down the four velocities you know: initial $0.48$ and $0.12\text{ m s}^{-1}$, final $0.30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ for B, and unknown $v$ for A. Multiply each by its mass from Table 3.1.
Hint 3: Set total before equal to total after and solve for $v$. If you get a negative value, think carefully about what that minus sign means for direction.
parts.proper_answer: Magnitude $0.060\text{ m s}^{-1}$, direction to the left, opposite to its initial velocity.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Apply Conservation of Momentum**
Take motion to the right as positive. No external resultant force acts, so total momentum is conserved:
$$m_A u_A + m_B u_B = m_A v_A + m_B v_B$$

Step 3: **Interpret the Sign**
The minus sign means the velocity is opposite to the positive direction you chose. So A rebounds and now moves to the left, opposite to its initial velocity and opposite to the final velocity of B.

parts.label: (c)
hints: Hint 1: Start with trolley A before the collision. What was its velocity from Table 3.1 and up to what time on Fig. 3.2 does it stay at that value?
Hint 2: Think about when A must finish changing its velocity. The two trolleys are in contact for the same time interval, so compare with the sloping section for B.
Hint 3: After the collision, what steady value from (b)(ii) should A hold up to $t = 0.50\text{ s}$, and how should you join the before and after sections?
parts.proper_answer: Horizontal line at $0.48\text{ m s}^{-1}$ from $t = 0$ to $t = 0.15\text{ s}$, straight line down to $-0.06\text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $t = 0.35\text{ s}$, then horizontal line at $-0.06\text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $t = 0.50\text{ s}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Draw the Before Part**
A approaches at constant $0.48\text{ m s}^{-1}$ until contact starts. From B's graph contact starts at $t = 0.15\text{ s}$. So draw a horizontal line from $(0, 0.48)$ to $(0.15, 0.48)$.

Step 2: **Draw the After Part**
After separation A moves steadily at $-0.060\text{ m s}^{-1}$ from (b)(ii). Contact ends at $t = 0.35\text{ s}$ when B becomes flat again. So draw a horizontal line from $(0.35, -0.06)$ to $(0.50, -0.06)$. Note it is below the time axis because direction reversed.

Step 3: **Join Them for the Collision**
During contact A slows down and reverses, so velocity falls steadily. Draw a straight line joining $(0.15, 0.48)$ to $(0.35, -0.06)$. It must start and end at exactly the same times as B's sloping section because they are in contact with each other.
